fill.approach: Start at the Dingford Creek Trailhead and hike the Dingford Creek Trail about 3.2 miles to the junction with the Hester Lake Trail. Leave the Myrtle Lake branch there and take the Hester Lake side, then leave the path and work cross-country toward the mountain's southwest ridge. Expect brush, steep forest and route-finding with no maintained tread.
fill.beta: The ridge is reached from the Hester Lake side rather than from Myrtle Lake. It is an off-trail line with bushwhacking and navigation; no detailed written description or reliable grade was found, so treat the difficulty as unknown and scout carefully.
watch_out: No established route description: difficulty and hazards on the ridge are unverified, so be ready to turn back
Long brushy off-trail approach where losing the line is easy
